text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe and South Africa reiterated the need to speed up talks aimed at reaching a new trade agreement, a joint commission of the two neighbours said at the end of a two-day meeting in Harare on Tuesday. The two have been negotiating a new pact since the expiry in 1992 of a 1964 preferential trade agreement.

- More than 330 Zimbabwean cattle rustlers were arrested and convicted in the first six months of this year, but stocktheft declined by 38 percent during the period compared to last year, police reported. Zimbabwe's Commercial Cattle Producers Association commended the police but said the recovery rate was still low.

- Zimbabwean Home Affairs Minister Dumiso Dabengwa on Tuesday denied charges by a parliamentary committee that his ministry's permanent secretary was inefficient and should be dismissed for financial mismanagement.
